-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

I am using `deno compile` in a package of a pnpm monorepo.  
It includes the entire monorepo, result in a huge size, I can't even run it.  
The binary output of bun is 55MB and 65MB for nodejs compile by `@yao-pkg/pkg`.

Command used `deno compile -A -o dist-backend/deno src/backend/deno.ts`

[![image](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/33727687/423780605-643f8f06-4de8-4de7-8985-a62b48b48470.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..oKyWCKo1quPcmsZarUN7jn7HSIMKHNsdF3o4D0Ou2Z4)](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/33727687/423780605-643f8f06-4de8-4de7-8985-a62b48b48470.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..oKyWCKo1quPcmsZarUN7jn7HSIMKHNsdF3o4D0Ou2Z4)

Is there an exclude option or some other tools that can prevent deno from bundling all the `node_modules` and unnecessary files?

I found the cause. It's because I have a deno workspace in the repo root. It bundles the entire workspace into the binary.  
But I couldn't find a way to workaround this.  
The only solution for me is to remove the deno workspace.

This is also a pnpm workspace, bun doesn't have issue with bundling binary.
